sources.role: official source archive; src/vm/m5/m5.h, m5.cpp, config.cpp, win32/winmain.cpp and win32/osd_input.cpp
official Windows x64 executable and distribution evidence
official Emu5 Win32 readme and key/ROM map

paths.naming: Win32 load_config/save_config call create_local_path("m5.ini"). The INI has [RecentFiles], [Screen], [Sound] and [Input]; [Input] persists JoyButtonsEx1_1..JoyButtonsEx8_16, UseJoyToKey, JoyToKeyType, JoyToKeyNumPad5 and JoyToKeyButtons1..16.

The native WinMM joystick backend enumerates joystick IDs 0..3 at runtime. JoyButtonsEx values encode (joystick_index << 5) | one of 32 direction/button/axis/POV bits; negative values in JoyToKeyButtons encode a Windows virtual key. keycode.cfg is an optional 256-byte VK-to-DIK conversion table, not a controller identity database. The official m5.txt map is FUNC=Tab, RESET=Backspace, joystick directions=Cursor, and triggers 1/5 (joystick 1) and 2/6 (joystick 2).

paths.path: The user-selected cartridge and tape files; no Emu5 battery-save sidecar is written by the reviewed m5 VM.
paths.naming: Cartridge ROM is read into the emulated $2000-$6FFF region. Tape playback/recording uses the path selected by the Win32 file dialog, so guest persistence is media-defined.

Ten Win32 menu slots call state_file_path(n), which formats <CONFIG_NAME>.sta<n>. The file is a Common Source Code Project FILEIO stream (outer state version 3, config-state version 8, m5 VM state version 4; gzip is used when built with zlib), so it is version/build-bound rather than a portable interchange format.
The m5 VM reads IPL.ROM as its 8 KiB internal ROM at $0000-$1FFF. The official source does not publish a canonical checksum for this user-supplied ROM.

paths.path: No cryptographic or firmware-key file is used by Emu5.
paths.naming: keycode.cfg is an input scan-code conversion table and is documented under input, not a decryption key.

windows.notes: The official x64 artifact is a PE32+ Windows executable. Lunchbox has no verified native controller writer for this Windows-only target; it must not modify a user's m5.ini or keycode.cfg.

linux.reason: The official Common Source Code Project distribution provides Windows Win32/x64 artifacts and source with a Win32 frontend, but no verified native Linux Emu5 package.

linux-flatpak.reason: No official Emu5 Flatpak package or manifest is published by the Common Source Code Project.

macos.reason: The official Common Source Code Project distribution provides Windows Win32/x64 artifacts and no verified native macOS Emu5 package.
